newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-WARNE BURST HALTS ENGLAND RECOVERY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-WARNE BURST HALTS ENGLAND RECOVERY.

text.p: Australian leg spinner Shane Warne took on his usual role as Ashes destroyer-in-chief on Friday to put the brakes on a brief England fightback on the second day of the fifth test at Trent Bridge.

After restricting Australia to 427 all out on an almost perfect batting pitch, England openers Mike Atherton and Alec Stewart put on 106 before Warne struck with three wickets for 14 in the space 40 balls.
At the close England were 188 for four, still 239 behind on first innings, and with Australia needing only a draw to retain the Ashes it looks all over for the hosts.
Things looked better for England in the afternoon when wicketkeeper Stewart led the way with the bat, thrashing 87 from 107 balls.

But Warne, so often the thorn in England's side, accounted for Stewart and Atherton (27), both caught by Ian Healy behind the stumps. Atherton was Healy's 300th test match dismissal -- 100 of them coming against England.
Warne then bowled Nasser Hussain for two and John Crawley gave Healy his third catch, this time off Glenn McGrath, as England collapsed to 141 for four.
Surrey team mates Graham Thorpe and Adam Hollioake steadied the ship in an unbeaten stand of 47 but it appeared too little too late for England who have not held the Ashes since 1989.

"We had five good hours today but the one hour after tea was disappointing, said Stewart. "I was just disappointed not to get a hundred. I tried to play in a controlled way against Shane but unfortunately I succumbed in the end."

Healy acknowledged the importance of Warne, saying: "We're a different team with and without him. It gives you so much confidence. There's a set of footmarks outside the stumps and there's only one bowler in the world who can use them."
England will have been satisfied to have restricted the touring team to 427 after they had begun the day on 302 for three.
The home bowlers persevered well in hot, humid conditions which offered some movement.
Mark Waugh was first to go, having added only eight to his overnight 60. He was trapped leg before by Caddick, ending a partnership of 86 with his twin brother Steve.
Three overs later Ricky Ponting played on to Headley for nine and then paceman Devon Malcolm dismissed Healy (16), Warne (nought) and Steve Waugh (75).
Headley cleaned up the tail soon after lunch to finish with four wickets for the third time in his three test appearances.
